title: Examining Human-AI Collaboration for Co-Writing Constructive Comments Online

bias_targets.methodology: Conducting forced-choice experiments to compare the LLM's preference for logical versus dialectical argumentation styles in evaluating constructiveness against the preferences of human raters.

Comparing linguistic features and homogenization metrics of LLM-assisted comments written by participants from collectivist (India) and individualistic (US) cultures to evaluate whether the LLM erases cultural nuances in argumentation.

Comparing sentiment and toxicity scores of users' original comment drafts with the LLM-rewritten suggestions to evaluate if the model alters the user's intended nuance by forcing an overly positive or moderate tone.

Measuring cosine similarity, semantic similarity, and ROUGE-L scores among independent human-written comments and human-AI co-written comments to assess if LLM assistance reduces textual and perspective diversity.
